title: How I Fell in with the Curate
question: Is there any hope left against them?
light: low sun from the west, long black shadows

pit.described: the great sand pit on Horsell Common in the late afternoon of 1894, a wide shallow crater of raw yellow sand in a waste of blackened heather and burnt-out cottages, a towering pillar of dense green smoke rising straight up out of the pit into the sky, and the crater's empty sandy rim at the right where the sentinel will stand; the light is the low late sun from the west at the LEFT, so the sand reads gold and the machine's long shadow lies black across the heather. Scorched fence posts and a charred cart lie at the pit's edge, and the far pine woods stand black and leafless on the skyline
pit.landmark_size: is the height of the frame
pit.route: from the burnt heather to the crater rim
pit.geometry: The raw yellow crater fills the BOTTOM half from the LEFT third to the RIGHT third, the pillar of green smoke rises from its CENTRE to the TOP edge, the sentinel fighting-machine stands on the crater rim at the RIGHT third, and blackened heather with burnt cottages runs to the low horizon across the TOP third at the LEFT. The charred cart lies at the BOTTOM LEFT and the black pine woods stand on the skyline at the TOP RIGHT.
pit.ambience: wind over burnt heath, distant crackling of small fires, a low mechanical hum

battery.described: a wooded hillside above the Thames near Richmond at twilight in 1894, a copse of beech trees with a black field gun hidden in its shade and its muzzle pointing out over the valley, two gunners in dark blue beside it, a row of suburban villas along the slope behind, and the flat valley below reaching away to a low horizon; the light is the last twilight glow from the west at the RIGHT, so the valley reads pale gold and the copse reads black. Stacked shells in wicker cases stand under the beeches and a limber waits with its horses among the trees
battery.landmark: the row of villas on the slope
battery.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
battery.route: from the copse out over the valley
battery.geometry: The black field gun stands in the shade of the beech copse at the LEFT third with its muzzle pointing to the CENTRE, two gunners stand beside it at the LEFT edge, the row of villas runs along the slope across the TOP third, and the pale valley reaches away at the RIGHT third to a low horizon. The stacked shell cases stand at the BOTTOM LEFT and the limber horses wait at the TOP LEFT.
battery.ambience: evening birdsong in beech trees, a horse stamping, distant voices of soldiers

river.described: the wide Thames below Shepperton in the hot afternoon of 1894 seen low from the water: grey-green water with pale steam drifting over it, a small abandoned rowing boat with empty rowlocks adrift at the centre, low reedy banks with willows on both sides and flat meadows beyond to a low horizon; the light is the hot afternoon sun from the west at the LEFT, so the steam reads white and the willows read black-green. Scorched lily pads float by the reeds and a drowned straw hat turns in the current
river.landmark_size: is a tenth of the height of the frame
river.route: from the water's surface down the river
river.geometry: The grey-green water fills the BOTTOM half from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, the small rowing boat drifts at the CENTRE, white steam drifts across the CENTRE, and the reedy banks with willows run along the TOP third on both sides. The drowned straw hat turns in the water at the BOTTOM RIGHT and lily pads float at the BOTTOM LEFT.
river.ambience: lapping river water, a faint hiss of steam, reeds rustling

halliford.described: riverside houses ON FIRE, flames bursting from their roofs and windows, the riverside of Halliford in the hot afternoon of 1894 seen from the water: a row of brick and timber houses facing the river, several of them burning, thin threads of orange flame and grey smoke going straight up into the still blue sky, the deserted towpath, dry reeds smoking along the bank, and a line of fire marching across a hay field beyond; the light is the hot afternoon sun from the west at the LEFT, so the flames read orange and the house fronts read dark red. A white garden gate stands open on the towpath and a swan drifts on the still water
halliford.landmark_size: is a third of the height of the frame
halliford.route: from the water along the riverfront
halliford.geometry: The river fills the BOTTOM third, the row of riverside houses stands across the CENTRE from the LEFT third to the RIGHT third with flames rising from the roofs at the CENTRE LEFT, the smoking reeds line the bank at the BOTTOM RIGHT, the deserted towpath runs along the LEFT third, and the line of fire crosses the hay field at the TOP third under the blue sky at the TOP edge.
halliford.ambience: crackling fire and falling timber, water lapping, far off a dog barking

bank.described: the Middlesex bank of the Thames near Walton in the late afternoon of 1894: long pale summer grass running down to the water, a few willows, the arches of Walton bridge coming into view round the bend downstream, and flat meadows behind to a low horizon; the light is the low afternoon sun from the west at the LEFT, so the grass reads gold and the willow shadows read black. Meadowsweet and dock grow along the water and a heron stands in the shallows
bank.landmark_size: is a fifth of the height of the frame
bank.route: from the long grass down to the water
bank.geometry: The long pale grass fills the BOTTOM half, the water runs across the CENTRE, the willows stand at the LEFT third, and the arches of Walton bridge stand on the bend at the RIGHT third under the sky at the TOP edge. The heron stands in the shallows at the CENTRE RIGHT and meadowsweet lines the water at the BOTTOM LEFT.
bank.ambience: insects in long grass, a lark high above, the river running

hedge.described: a field edge beside a tall hawthorn hedge near Walton at sunset in 1894: long summer grass, a narrow path running north along the hedge, the land dead flat to a low horizon, a flat far bank lined with tall elms across the river, and a mackerel sky of rows and rows of small plumed clouds tinted pink and gold by the sunset; the light is the low sunset from the west at the LEFT, so the clouds read rose and the hedge reads dark green-black. Poppies and ox-eye daisies stand in the grass along the hedge foot and a wooden stile crosses the path
hedge.landmark: the path running north beside the hedge
hedge.landmark_size: is a tenth of the height of the frame
hedge.route: from the hedge along the path

The wooden stile crosses the path at the CENTRE and poppies stand along the hedge foot at the BOTTOM LEFT.
hedge.ambience: evening crickets, a light breeze in the hawthorn, a distant cow lowing

source: What does it mean?
What do these things mean?

shots.why: The Martians went back to their pit, and a wall of guns rose against them.
source: the Martians retreated to their original position upon Horsell Common
above the blackened heather and ruined buildings that stretched far and wide, stood one as sentinel

sounds.sound: a deep metallic clanking of heavy machinery at work in a pit, far off

shots.frame: Medium in the late afternoon on the empty fighting-machines standing with folded legs on the crater rim, green smoke rising behind them.

shots.at_rest: The empty fighting-machines stand at the CENTRE on the crater rim with their long legs folded, the green smoke rising behind them at the TOP third, and a gentle slope of raw yellow sand runs down across the BOTTOM third. shots.why: They left the machines empty on the rim and went down into the pit.
source: the rest abandoned their vast fighting-machines and descended into the pit

source: every row of suburban villas on the hilly slopes about Kingston and Richmond, masked an expectant black muzzle
crawled the devoted scouts with the heliographs that were presently to warn the gunners

sounds.sound: a heavy iron field gun breech being closed, metal on metal

sounds.sound: water lapping against a small drifting wooden boat

source: I contrived to paddle, as well as my parboiled hands would allow

sounds.sound: a hand paddling in water beside a small wooden boat

sounds.sound: dry reeds crackling as they burn

source: as the bridge at Walton was coming into sight round the bend
my fever and faintness overcame my fears

We have chanced to come in for the thick of it

shots.frame: Insert at sunset on a small bright heliograph flicker winking above the far tree line across the river, under the rose mackerel sky.
shots.motion: The camera tracks beside the dark hedge top to the tree line already in the picture until the flicker stands at the right of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; the heliograph goes on flashing; the clouds go on darkening.
shots.camera: above the hedge at a standing man's eye, a 35mm lens. The sunset comes from the west at the LEFT; the clouds read rose and the elms read dark
shots.at_rest: The rose mackerel sky fills the TOP half, the elms of the flat far bank stand at the CENTRE as a dark line, and a small bright heliograph flicker winks above the far tree line at the RIGHT third, the dark hedge top at the BOTTOM edge. The river glints pale below the elms at the CENTRE, and a thin line of smoke lies along the far skyline at the LEFT third.
shots.why: That flicker was the heliograph, the sign of human help, of guns being placed.
source: I told him it was the heliograph signalling
where those hills rise about Richmond and Kingston and the trees give cover

shots.frame: Medium close at dusk on the head and shoulders of the curate (long pale face of fair weakness with a retreating chin and a small full mouth, soot-smudged white linen shirt sleeves under a black clerical waistcoat buttoned to a white anglican dog collar), risen, turned to the camera, one hand raised, stopping the talk, a faint crescent moon above a bank of smoke in the sky behind him.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward him with small amplitude until his head and raised hand fill the middle of the picture, travelling a hand's breadth; he whispers sharply; his head goes on turning toward the far bank.
shots.camera: in the grass level with his eyes, three paces from him, an 85mm lens. The dusk comes from the LEFT; his face reads pale and the hedge reads black
shots.at_rest: The curate's head and shoulders are at the CENTRE, turned to the camera, one hand raised beside his face at the RIGHT third, the dark hedge behind him at the LEFT third. His head is half the frame's height.
shots.why: 'Listen!' he said.
source: And even as I spoke he sprang to his feet and stopped me by a gesture
From beyond the low hills across the water came the dull resonance of distant guns

sounds.sound: the dull boom of distant artillery guns across a valley
a remote, weird, wailing mechanical cry far away in the dusk

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: What does it mean? What do these things mean?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Stung, the Martians fell back to their pit on Horsell Common, dragging their dead machine.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Had they pushed on, nothing but a few guns stood between them and London.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: They were in no hurry. And every hour, another gun was dug in.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I had found a boat, drifting empty down the steaming river.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: No oars. I paddled with my scalded hands, looking behind me all the way.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Halliford was deserted. The houses burned in silence, with no crowd to watch them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Inland, a line of fire marched across a field of hay.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At Walton bridge my fever beat my fear, and I crawled ashore.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I woke to a stranger beside me, staring at a flicker in the sky.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Have you any water?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He shook his head. I had been asking for water, he said, for an hour.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: What sins have we done?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A curate. After morning service he had walked out, into fire and death.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: What are we?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: His church, rebuilt three years ago, was gone. His whole parish, swept away.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: The smoke of her burning goeth up for ever and ever!

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Be a man!

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: They are pitiless.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: One of them was killed yonder, not three hours ago.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Killed? He stared about him, as if God's own ministers could not die.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I had seen it happen. We had simply come in for the thick of it.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: That flicker was a heliograph. Beyond those hills, men were placing guns.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: Listen!
